fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. "A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish…" (Isaiah 42:3) Both of those are things that are barely holding on. I think that's a gentle picture. The verse goes on, "He will faithfully bring forth justice."

Swapping them out is a clever guess, like grabbing a fresh box when one gets dented. But the verse doesn't have the Servant trading anything. It says, "A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish…" (Isaiah 42:3) He will not break the bruised reed, and He will not extinguish the smoldering wick.

That's it, friend. "In His law the islands will put their hope." (Isaiah 42:4) The islands are the ones who hope in His law. That comes right after the Servant will not grow weak or discouraged before He has established justice on the earth.
Deserts are a fair guess, baker. But the text doesn't name them. It says, "In His law the islands will put their hope." (Isaiah 42:4) So the answer is the islands.

Walls and bricks, I see where you went. That's a real job in another part of the Bible (Nehemiah 2:17), but it's not in this list. Isaiah 42:7 names these jobs: "…to open the eyes of the blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon and those sitting in darkness out from the prison house."
Temple is a reasonable guess. But it's not what the verse says. The LORD says, "I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols." (Isaiah 42:8) The word you want is praise.
People is a fair guess, friend. But that's not what Isaiah 42:8 says. The LORD says, "I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols." What He won't give to idols is His praise.

Yes, baker. "Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things." (Isaiah 42:9) The old things are done, and the LORD is announcing something new. The verse adds, "Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you."

Hidden has a nice mysterious ring to it. But the verse doesn't say that. It says, "Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things." (Isaiah 42:9) The LORD is declaring new things, not hidden ones.
